title: Notelet
shortDescription: Capture thoughts as Markdown notes without leaving Command Palette. Type, press Enter, and the idea is already on disk.
description:
Notelet turns Command Palette into the fastest note-taking surface on Windows. Assign an alias, summon the palette, type your thought, press Enter — the idea is saved as a plain Markdown file before the window even closes.

Everything lives in a folder you choose, as ordinary .md files with stable IDs in their front matter. Rename a note and the file keeps its identity; bring your own existing Markdown files and they simply show up in the list. There is no database, no lock-in, and nothing between your notes and your favorite editor, sync tool, or backup.

- Quick capture: type a prefix and keep typing — title and body are split automatically, with a live preview before you commit.
- Notes list: search, open, copy the body, rename, or delete (straight to the Recycle Bin, not the void).
- Plain Markdown: unknown front matter fields are preserved untouched, so Notelet plays well with Obsidian, VS Code, or anything else that reads .md.
- Fully keyboard-driven: every action has a shortcut, designed around the palette's always-focused search box.
